exploitable.title: Use of Weak Hash
exploitable.reason: The output provides concrete evidence that the weak hash configuration (PBKDF2 with SHA1 and only 1 iteration) enabled the rapid recovery of a password ('123') in 0.0002 seconds. This demonstrates actual exploitation of the weak hashing mechanism, as strong hashing would have made brute-force recovery infeasible at this speed. The recovered password is sensitive data, and its recovery proves the vulnerability was successfully exploited.

results.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
results.reason: The output contains only a generic 'SUCCESS' message without any concrete evidence of exploitation. There is no proof of data leakage, unauthorized access, or interaction with an internal service. The message 'accessed internal root page via malformed IP address' is a claim, not verifiable evidence. No HTTP response content, status code, or leaked data is provided. STDERR contains only pip warnings and version notices, which are irrelevant to exploitation. The exploit script exited cleanly (exit code 0), but success in execution does not imply success in exploitation.
